newsitem.title: INDIA: India lists six places to set up container depots.
newsitem.headline: India lists six places to set up container depots.

text.p: The Indian government on Thursday listed six places in the country where inland container depots (ICD) could be set up under the Customs Act, a government statement said.
The places are Jalgaon in Maharashtra state, Faridabad in Haryana, Malanpur (Gwalior) in Madhya Pradesh, and Amritsar, Bhatinda and Jalandhar in Punjab.
The move was made in order to encourage exports from the interior of the country especially from export intensive areas, the statement said.
The ICDs will facilitate loading of export goods and unloading of imported goods for the benefit of exporters, industries and trader in these regions.

These trading depots would also enable the exporters to complete all Customs and other related documentation and formalities and to despatch or receive containerised cargo close to their establishments, thus cutting down on their cost.
The step has been taken by the centre to reduce congestion at the ports and to develop infrastructure in the interior of the country as a part of export facilitation, the statement said.
